outcome: Development of placental layers (decidual, junction, labyrinth)
cohort: 30 female Specific Pathogen Free mice with unilateral uterine scarring (simulating a cesarean section) and contralateral uteruses used as control.
finding: Scarred uteruses in mice demonstrated reduced blastocyst implantation, decreased endometrial receptivity (lower pinopode coverage, decreased Lif mRNA, increased MUC1 mRNA), and excessive trophoblast invasion during placental development.
mod_finding: The simulation of a cesarean section leading to a scarred uterus was associated with reduced endometrial receptivity and excessive trophoblast invasion in mice.
followup_time: 4.5 days, 13.5 days, 15.5 days, 17.5 days, and 18.5 days after conception
gest_age: 4.5 days (window of implantation), 13.5 days, 15.5 days, 17.5 days (placental formation), and 18.5 days (mature placenta) after conception
